subject: Clarify microcall billing boundaries and partial-token rounding
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T15:18:00-08:00
Subject: Question on microcall billing and partial-token rounding

Hi Avery,

Quick follow-up from our invoice review (see attached sample-invoice.pdf). A couple of line items look like they're driven by many very short calls from our mobile app (microcalls that average ~14 tokens generated). The invoice shows those rounded up to the next 256-token slab which materially increased the line item.

Two specific asks:
- How does Redwood currently meter and round extremely short calls that still have a nontrivial prefix (session context + routing metadata)?
- If we enable model-fallback (smaller model then fallback to larger on low-confidence), how are the tokens attributed across models and do we get charged per model separately or as a single aggregated session?

We'd like an explanation and a proposal for a pragmatic concession for a pilot month while we optimize the client-side batching.

Thanks,
Samira
Director of Product
BrightCart

[Attachment: sample-invoice.pdf (pdf)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>
Cc: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on microcall billing and partial-token rounding

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear notes and the invoice extract. This is a great, concrete example. TL;DR: current default meter is per-request token accounting with a per-call quantum used for invoice aggregation; model-fallback charges are attributed to the model that served each token (so multi-model paths can produce multiple line items unless a routing aggregation rule applies).

Longer explanation and proposal below.

How we currently meter microcalls
- Token accounting: we count input + output tokens per request.
- Aggregation quantum: for low-volume microcalls we aggregate into a billing quantum (default 256 tokens) to avoid noise on invoices. That aggregation is per-session prefix when requests share the same conversation id and model family.
- Model-fallback behavior: tokens are billed to the model instance that produced them. If a single request triggers a quick smaller-model reply then a fallback to a larger model, you'll see both models on the usage report. We do offer an opt-in aggregation rule for fallbacks (bundle as single logical request) but it's not enabled by default.

Concession & short pilot option (what I can offer quickly)
- Pilot concession for 30 days: for the BrightCart pilot we can:
  * Apply a microcall quantum of 8 tokens for calls where the generated tokens <= 32 and the request TTL is under 300ms (heuristic for true microcalls).
  * Enable fallback aggregation for requests tagged with your conversation_id header so we bill as a single logical request (tokens still count, but the line item is consolidated).
  * Issue a one-time invoice credit equivalent to the difference between default-256 rounding and the microcall-quantum on your November invoice (estimate attached).

If you're amenable I will loop in our billing team to size the credit and have Ben confirm the invoice adjustment. I've attached a short commit-matrix that shows the math for one sample day.

Next step: confirm you want the pilot concession and provide the conversation_id pattern (or we can suggest a header to pass).

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery@redwood.com

[Attachment: commit-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T20:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Question on microcall billing and partial-token rounding — need billing approval

Ben / Vanessa — forwarding BrightCart's ask and my proposed pilot concession. They have a cluster of short mobile calls that are being aggregated into the 256-token billing quantum and it's inflating the November line item.

Key numbers (from the attached matrix):
- Example day: 12,400 microcalls, avg generated tokens per call = 14, input tokens ~ 8.
- Current billing after aggregation (256 quantum) = 12,400 * 256 tokens billed = 3,174,400 token-units.
- With 8-token microcall quantum (pilot) we'd bill 12,400 * 8 = 99,200 token-units.
- Net difference (tokens billed) = 3,075,200 token-units (~98% reduction for that pattern) — we propose to credit the delta for the pilot month only.

Operational asks for billing to implement pilot:
1) Approve microcall quantum = 8 tokens for requests matching header "X-BC-Microcall: 1" and generated_tokens <= 32.
2) Enable fallback aggregation where request contains "X-BC-Conversation: <pattern>" so fallback isn't split into multiple invoice lines.
3) Calculate credit amount for November invoice and provide an invoice adjustment ID we can reference in the DocuSign amendment.

If you approve I will send the customer an updated DocuSign with the pilot terms.

Thanks — Avery

[Attachment: sample-invoice.pdf (pdf)]

From: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>

Please proceed with billing authorization and send the DocuSign amendment that references the invoice adjustment ID once Ben provides it. If possible, can we get the pilot credit reflected on the November invoice prior to the month-end close? That will help our finance team reconcile.

Thanks again — Samira
Director of Product, BrightCart
